slides.head:
Ten AI experiments from Adobe
could reach your edit next.
Ten projects, one night.
slides.body: At Adobe MAX in Miami Beach on November 11, Adobe previewed ten research projects in its Sneaks session. They are research previews, not products, and no ship dates were given.

slides.head: One edit, every angle.
slides.body: Scene Sweep tracks characters, locations and scenes across a sequence and applies one edit across cuts and camera angles. Live Set changes subject, setting or camera mid-scene.

slides.head: Timing you can draw.
slides.body: On Cue sets when an action happens in generated video, from a line drawn by hand or timing taken from video or music. Sound Bender lifts a described sound out of a finished mix.

slides.head: Two you can try today.
slides.body: Deep Brush and Hands On are live in the Adobe Labs Playground. Adobe says about half of the projects it shows each year end up in its final software.

slides.head: Control is the new prompt.
slides.body: These tools trade typing for brushes, drags and timing marks. The software is moving toward how editors already work, so the craft of directing a shot matters more, not less.
